The text contrasts two opposing views on human nature. William Golding’s *Lord of the Flies* presents the theme that evil is inherent within humans, as evidenced by the boys' descent into savagery when removed from societal constraints. In contrast, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy suggests that society is the corrupting force, implying that humanity’s natural state is inherently good and free. The similarity lies in both texts addressing the fundamental nature of humanity and the factors that influence moral behavior. The difference lies in their conclusions: Golding argues that evil is internal and innate, while Rousseau argues that goodness is innate and corrupted by external societal structures.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
